stb_001: You can recognise them by the ring of six trees around the old circular stone tank and fountain, the tallest classified trees in the city. They stand in Largo Jose Afonso.
stb_002: You can recognise it by its crown covering the entire small square, turning the whole space into a room of shade. It stands in Largo Doutor Francisco Soveral.
stb_004: You can recognise it by its low, sprawling dome of branches running almost horizontally from the base, walked under rather than looked up at. It stands in the Jardim Engenheiro Luis da Fonseca.
stb_006: You can recognise it by its leaves split into several separate leaflets rather than one lobed blade, often mistaken for an ash. It stands in the Jardim do Bonfim.
stb_007: You can recognise it by its neat, dense pyramid shape and pale pink cup-shaped flowers in summer. It stands on Rua Oliveira Martins, Montalvao.
stb_009: You can recognise it in autumn and winter by clusters of small, bright red drupes hanging from an otherwise unremarkable street tree. It stands on Avenida Manuel Maria Portela.
stb_010: You can recognise it by its long, drooping leaves hanging almost to the ground, forming a green tent to stand under. It stands alone in the Jardim de Palhais, Sao Sebastiao.
